newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares slip but support holding.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares slip but support holding.

text.p: Austrian shares trudged lower on Thursday, taking their cue from a weak international lead, but the blue-chip ATX index managed to hold above the psychologically significant 1,200-points level.
"The underlying mood in the market is fairly positive. Investors are biding their time and I would not be surprised to see prices pick up next week," said a trader.
The ATX ended 4.19 points, or 0.35 percent, down at 1,209.50 with 14 issues off, six up and one unchanged.
March ATX futures, which go off the board on Friday, stood six points down at 1,207 points. Dealers forecast an expiry between 1,200 and 1,220.
"I don't expect to many fireworks tomorrow. The open interest is pretty small," said one.
Beverages group BBAG was the day's leading gainer. Its shares rose 7.5 schillings, or one percent, to 760 schillings.
Lower Austrian utility EVN also advanced on brisk turnover, finishing 15.4 schillings up at 1,691.7.
Points maker VAE closed 12 schillings higher at 1,165 after reporting a rise in 1996 pre-tax earnings and a steady 32 schillings dividend payment despite a fall in net profit.
Engineering group VA Technologie was the biggest decliner. Its shares fell 32 schillings, or 1.81 percent, to 1,733 schillings.

Water treatment firm BWT dropped 24 schillings to 1,415 on profit-taking after a strong run that had taken the stock 10 percent higher since Friday. The firm announced last week it expected higher earnings from new technology.
The all-share Vienna bourse index was 0.59 points down at 454.2. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 254
